We need to adapt to include parameterized tests, use Mockito for mocking trades where needed (null fields). The framework uses real Trade objects for many cases, but for null fields we may need to mock Trade to return null for amount/value etc. Also for null entry trade we need a Position where entry is null but isOpened() true? How to create such a Position? The Position class constructors: there is a default constructor (no args) and a constructor Position(Trade entry, Trade exit, CostModel transactionModel, CostModel holdingModel). Also a constructor Position(Trade.TradeType startingType, CostModel transactionModel, CostModel holdingModel). The default constructor likely creates empty position (no entry). The isOpened() method likely returns true if entry != null && exit == null? Not sure. But to simulate null entry, we could create Position via default constructor then use reflection to set entry field to null (already null). But isOpened() may return false if entry null. The test case expects NullPointerException when entry is null but isOpened() true. That scenario might be unrealistic but we can force by mocking Position subclass? Maybe we can use reflection to set entry to null and also set a flag that isOpened() returns true (maybe based on exit null). If entry null, isOpened() might be false. So we need to mock Position? Using Mockito we can spy Position and stub isOpened() true, entry null. But entry is private field; we can use reflection to set entry to null and ensure isOpened() returns true (maybe isOpened() checks entry != null). If entry null, isOpened() false, so method would go to else branch (closed) and use exit which may be null causing NPE but not the same scenario. But test expects NPE due to entry null when opened. So we need to create a Position where entry is null but isOpened() returns true. Could achieve via subclass of Position overriding isOpened() to return true, and entry null. But we cannot modify Position class. However we can create a mock of Position using Mockito, but we need to call real method getGrossProfit on mock? Use spy and stub entry to null? Let's inspect typical implementation of isOpened() in Position (not provided). Usually isOpened() returns entry != null && exit == null. So with entry null, isOpened() false. So the method would go to else branch, using exit which is also null, causing NPE at exit.getValue(). That still yields NPE but not due to entry. The test description expects NPE due to entry null. Might be okay whichever NPE occurs. We'll just test that NPE is thrown.

Similarly for null exit trade when closed.

But need entry null and isOpened true? Not possible; but we can call getGrossProfit on Position with entry null and exit null; method will go to else branch (closed) and attempt exit.getValue() causing NPE. That's still NPE.
